verification.summary: AL BAHYAH, a very large crude carrier owned by ADNOC Logistics and Services, was struck by projectiles in the early hours of 14 July 2026 while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, 13 nautical miles from the coast of Oman. The owner said both Al Bahyah and the time-chartered VLCC Mombasa B were hit, that one seafarer lost his life and several others were injured, and that both ships were significantly damaged. The IMO confirmed incident register records one seafarer fatality and three injured on Al Bahyah, and eleven injured on Mombasa B. The UAE Ministry of Defence attributed the strikes to two Iranian cruise missiles and said the seafarer who died was aboard Mombasa B and was of Indian nationality. Oman's Maritime Security Centre said 18 Al Bahyah crew were rescued and three remained missing.

verification.summary: MAYUREE NAREE, a Thai-flagged bulk carrier owned by Precious Shipping, was struck by two projectiles of unknown origin about 11 nautical miles north of Oman on 11 March 2026 while in ballast from Khalifa Port towards India. The projectiles hit above the waterline, set the engine room on fire and left it flooded. Twenty of the 23 Thai crew were taken off with help from the Omani navy and flew home on 16 March, and three were trapped in the engine room. A search team hired by Precious Shipping found human remains in the damaged area, as Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported on 3 April 2026, and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow confirmed on 8 April that all three had died. Their remains were repatriated to Thailand in early July.
verification.date_note: The strike was reported on 11 March in Gulf local time, which is UTC+4, so the UTC date is also 11 March; no exact event time was published.

verification.summary: MUSSAFAH 2, an Emirati flagged salvage tug operated by Abu Dhabi Ports, was hit by two missiles at about 02:00 local time on 6 March 2026 while preparing to tow the abandoned container ship SAFEEN PRESTIGE, which had been struck two days earlier. UKMTO reported an incident six nautical miles north of Oman in which a tug was hit by unknown projectiles, and the IMO confirmed incident register records four seafarer fatalities and three severely injured on this ship that day. The tug caught fire and sank. Indonesia's foreign ministry said the tug had seven crew from Indonesia, India and the Philippines, that four survived and that three Indonesians were missing. The Migrant Workers Office of the Philippine Embassy in Abu Dhabi said the second missile hit the bridge, where four crew including the only Filipino on board were standing, and that all four were missing and presumed dead.
verification.date_note: UKMTO 015-26, the IMO register and the owner linked reporting all give the attack as 6 March 2026. Initial reports spoke of eight crew aboard while Indonesia's foreign ministry gave seven, and about thirteen people were on the tug and the container ship together, so the crew total is recorded as reported rather than reconciled. The Indonesian ministry's toll of four survivors and three missing sits beside the IMO toll of four dead and three severely injured; the two are kept side by side and not merged.

The register keeps four seafarer fatalities and three severely injured, and the injured snapshot is now dated to the attack rather than to the register check. The sinking and the crew breakdown are taken from Agence France-Presse quoting Indonesia's foreign ministry, which reported seven crew from Indonesia, India and the Philippines and three Indonesians missing. updates.text: Crew nationalities added to a record that carried four deaths with no nationality detail. The IMO register confirms four seafarer fatalities and three severely injured on this tug. Indonesia's foreign ministry named three Indonesian crew members, including the captain, as missing, and the Philippine Embassy's Migrant Workers Office in Abu Dhabi reported that the second missile struck the bridge where four crew including the only Filipino on board were standing and that all four were missing and presumed dead. On that basis the four deaths are recorded as three Indonesian and one Filipino: the four men reported missing are the four fatalities in the IMO total. The two authorities disagree on the structure of the toll, the ministry giving four survivors and three missing while the IMO gives four dead and three severely injured, and that conflict is left visible rather than averaged. No nationality is inferred from the tug's Emirati flag or from any crew list. No image is added.

verification.location_text: About 70NM east of Byala, inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone
verification.summary: ABLE, a Palau flagged general cargo ship of 7,416 deadweight built in 1991 and Turkish owned, was attacked by air and sea drones about 70 nautical miles east of Byala, inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, in the early hours of 6 October 2026 while carrying barley from Romania to Turkey. A fire broke out and the engine room began to fill with water. Bulgaria's Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the ferry Dioscuria, the navy and the border police rescued all 18 crew, 11 Turkish and 7 Indian; two were injured in the fire and taken to Varna for treatment. The ship stayed afloat, left the Bulgarian zone on 14 October and, according to Nova Televizia as reported by Sofia Globe, disappeared from radar late on 19 October and sank off the Turkish coast.
verification.date_note: Bulgarian officials placed the attack at about 03:00 local time on 6 October 2026; the BBC gives 23:00 GMT. The record keeps 6 October, the date used by the Bulgarian government and by the Bulgarian and international reporting checked.

The injured snapshot of two is dated 6 October 2026. Deaths stay zero for this ship: nobody on the Able is reported dead. The crew of the Alfa Watan, the other ship attacked in the same incident, are recorded under that ship and are not counted here. verification.summary: HS Dignity, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged general cargo ship with 16 people aboard, was struck by a drone at about 01:20 local time on 13 October and sank 17 nautical miles east of Shabla, Bulgaria. Four survivors were taken aboard AZOV CONCORD and a fifth by the Danish-flagged SCANDI ASSERTER; Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications declared the search and rescue operation over at 15:00 on 14 October.
verification.date_note: Local Bulgarian time is UTC+3, so 01:20 on 13 October falls at 22:20 UTC on 12 October; the ministry and the Bulgarian News Agency date the sinking 13 October and the day-precision UTC date is kept as reported, not recalculated.

updates.text: First reviewed living record for this sinking. Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications reported six crew rescued and 10 unaccounted for when the search ended on 14 October; Bulgarian outlets and the Syrian Sailors Union reported five rescued and 11 missing, and 24 Chasa said the fifth survivor reached Varna later on another ship. Because the rescued and missing split is unresolved, no missing figure is recorded as a snapshot and no death is counted. The ministry places the sinking 17 nautical miles east of Shabla; some reports say 15 to 17 miles east of Krapets. No nationality is recorded for the missing: Syria's Foreign Ministry told SANA on 18 October that 14 Syrians and two Egyptians were aboard, while other accounts gave 12 Syrians, and crew nationality is not inferred from the flag.

updates.text: New historical record for an event absent from both incident stores. Two unladen cargo ships bound for Rostov-on-Don were struck by drones in Taganrog Bay in the north eastern Sea of Azov shortly after midnight on 5 June 2026, and the five deaths are split between two records rather than counted twice. 2 of the five dead were aboard NATRA, according to the Taman maritime rescue and coordination centre report carried by Azerbaijan's Operative Information Centre, and 3 were aboard HIST-BS-20260605-CIRCON, so the two records together account for the five deaths Azerbaijan's foreign ministry reported and not for ten. verification.summary: CONTSHIP JET, a Liberia flagged container ship carrying 421 containers from Haifa in Israel to Constanta in Romania, was struck by three sea drones on 28 October 2026 about 17 nautical miles east of Cape Kaliakra inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. The maritime rescue coordination centre at Constanta was alerted at 12:01 local time and the 18 crew left the ship at 12:13; eight were taken aboard a Bulgarian Navy boat and the other ten were in the ship's lifeboat, and all 18 were rescued and taken towards Varna for medical checks. Bulgarian defence minister Dimitar Stoyanov announced the attack at a briefing in Sofia with the Romanian and Turkish defence ministers, and the three countries condemned the drone attacks on commercial vessels. The crew were 14 Filipinos and 4 Ukrainians. No death was reported among the 18. No party claimed the attack and no authority attributed it.

Local Bulgarian time was EET (UTC+2) after the clock change on 25 October, and the day is kept as reported rather than recalculated.

Bulgaria's Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the ferry Dioscuria, the navy and the border police rescued all 18 crew, 11 Turkish and 7 Indian; two were injured in the fire and taken to Varna for treatment. verification.date_note: Bulgarian officials placed the attack at about 03:00 local time on 6 October 2026; the BBC gives 23:00 GMT. The record keeps 6 October, the date used by the Bulgarian government and by the Bulgarian and international reporting checked.

verification.summary: KHORYV, a Comoros-flagged ore/oil carrier of 3,280 dwt built in 1983, was 13 nautical miles off Constanta en route from Eregli to Sulina when it sent a distress signal at about 10:00 local time on 23 October 2026 and caught fire. Romania's Naval Authority said the 13 crew were 10 Ukrainian and 3 Azerbaijani nationals, that intervention vessels recovered nine people alive and one body from the water, and that three crew were still missing while the search continued in poor weather. The ship capsized and lay upside down, and Romanian hydrographic warning ARN 153/2026 gave its position as 44 06.59 N 029 01.10 E. Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the dead seafarer was a Ukrainian citizen, that four Ukrainians including the master were taken to hospital and that two Ukrainians needed no medical treatment. Romania's president, Nicusor Dan, said the vessel had been struck by a drone; the naval authority's statement did not establish the cause.
verification.date_note: Romanian local time on 23 October is UTC+3, so the 10:00 distress call was about 07:00 UTC on the same day. The day-precision UTC date is kept as reported.

One missile hit the starboard side of the superstructure and a fire broke out. Seventeen people were on board, including five Indian nationals and a Ukrainian port pilot. Ten were killed: nine crew, among them four Indian seafarers, and the Ukrainian pilot. Eight survivors were rescued. Ukraine's seaports authority and the ship's managers reported that the vessel sank off Odesa on 26 July 2026. Ukraine's Air Force and navy attributed the strike to Russia; Russia's defence ministry said ships in the area were carrying military cargo, while India said GOLDEN LEO had loaded grain.
verification.date_note: Day precision from India's Ministry of External Affairs statement of 20 July 2026, which places the attack on the evening of 19 July. The Hindu reports the strike at about 16:00 Ukraine local time. Seatrade names the departure port as Chornomorsk in the Odesa region; the Ministry of External Affairs says the port of Odesa.

A fire broke out, crude oil burned on the water and thick black smoke closed beaches at Sirius. The 23 crew members, all Indian nationals according to Russia's Transport Ministry, abandoned the vessel and were rescued by the Sochi port authority. verification.location_text: Bystre sea approach channel, Danube delta near Vylkove, Odesa region, Ukraine
verification.attack_type: Explosion of an unidentified explosive device in the channel; a mine is suspected in Ukrainian reporting, and no attacker is established
verification.summary: The Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority states that at about 22:30 on 23 July 2025 its dredger INGULSKY, IMO 9646912, flag Ukraine, owned by the state enterprise's Delta-pilot branch, exploded on an unidentified explosive device in the Bystre sea approach channel. The vessel was holed and sank partially to starboard. Of the 11 crew on board, three died and eight were rescued, four of them injured, according to the authority's detailed account. DredgingToday reported the authority's confirmation that three crew members died and that the others were taken to hospital, and noted that local media suggested a naval mine while the cause remained under investigation. Ukrainian reporting in February 2026 recorded that the authority had named small survey boats after the three dead employees and said the dredger struck a mine; the same report said the vessel was raised in September 2025. The sources do not identify an attacker.
verification.date_note: Day precision only. The authority gives about 22:30 local time on 23 July 2025; Ukrainian local time was UTC+3 that day, so the explosion was about 19:30 UTC on the same date. The tracker keeps the reported calendar date.

update.text: New historical record for a Black Sea event that was held pending reconciliation. The Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority and later Ukrainian reporting establish that the state-owned dredger INGULSKY, IMO 9646912, exploded on an unidentified device in the Bystre approach channel on 23 July 2025 with 11 crew on board, and that three crew members died. Deaths are recorded as three, not as a minimum, because the authority's account and the two later reports agree on that figure. The dredger is a state-owned port authority workboat rather than a trading cargo ship, and it is recorded here as a dredger so that it is not read as part of the merchant cargo fleet.

update.text: Follow-up on a record first reviewed on 26 October. Three things are added and the count does not change. India's Ministry of External Affairs said the two seafarers killed were foreign nationals, so neither death was Indian, and that all three Indian crew members were safe with one of them injured; that is the first authority statement ruling out an Indian fatality here and it is why no Indian nationality entry exists. update.text: Corpus cross-check so that this attack is not counted twice. The corpus carries the same 28 October attack a second time as INC-20261028-011, from a Romanian report describing a Greek-flagged vessel hit by drones near the Bulgarian coast. Reuters reported the vessel badly damaged and listing but afloat, with the owner confirming that all 18 crew, 14 Filipinos and four Ukrainians, were safe and ashore. The reviewed identity, date, zero deaths and the crew breakdown already recorded here are unchanged; no injury was reported, and the state of the ship after 28 October was not established by any source read today.
